title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement: You get a list of integers that may include negatives and zeros. A subarray is a run of neighbouring elements. Find the largest product you can get by multiplying all the numbers of one non-empty subarray, and return that product.

example.caption: The subarray [2, 3] multiplies to 6, the best of all runs. Including -2 would make it negative.

idea.sentence: Track both the biggest and the smallest product of a subarray ending at i, because multiplying by a negative number turns the smallest into the biggest.

jargon.plain: A run of neighbouring elements. Unlike a subsequence, you cannot skip any in the middle.
Build each answer from the answer just before it, stored in a table.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of integers, e.g. [2,3,-2,4]

vars.meaning: number of integers in the list

compare.optimalLabel: One pass with two cells per index

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Start at every index and keep multiplying to the right, tracking the biggest.

rows.name: hi and lo tables
rows.note: Two cells per index, each built from the two cells just before it.

rows.name: Two running variables
rows.note: Only the previous hi and lo are read, so keep two numbers instead of two arrays.

fast.takeaway: A running best is not enough. A very negative product is dangerous to drop, since one more negative makes it the winner.

stages.title: First cell
stages.note: A subarray of one number is that number, so hi[0] and lo[0] are both nums[0].

stages.title: Biggest ending here
stages.note: hi[i] is the biggest of x alone, x times the old hi, and x times the old lo.

stages.title: Smallest ending here
stages.note: lo[i] is the smallest of the same three. It is kept because a later negative can flip it.

stages.title: Answer
stages.note: The best subarray ends at some index, so the answer is the biggest hi in the table.

edges.title: Single negative
edges.why: The subarray must be non-empty, so the answer can be negative. Start best at nums[0], not at 0.

edges.title: Two negatives cancel
edges.why: hi alone would give 3. The old lo of -6, times -4, becomes 24.

edges.title: Zero cuts the run
edges.why: Zero times anything is zero, but x alone is always a candidate, so the next element starts fresh.

edges.title: Only zeros
edges.why: Every product is 0. The answer 0 comes from the table, not from a default.

gotchas.text: Keeping only a running max is the classic bug. After [-2, 3, -4] the max chain would be 3, but the answer is 24 because of the -6 you threw away.
Include x alone as a candidate. That is how a zero, or a long bad run, resets the subarray.
Multiplying 0 by a negative gives -0, and Math.min can return it. It compares equal to 0 with ===, so answers are fine, but Object.is(-0, 0) is false.
Products overflow int past about 9.2e18. The usual limits keep this safe. For long inputs of large numbers, use math/big or compare in log space.

recap.key: hi[i] and lo[i] are the biggest and smallest product ending at i. Each is the max or min of x, x times old hi, x times old lo.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(n), or O(1) with two variables.
moves: For each x, compute x times old hi and x times old lo
hi = max of the three, lo = min of the three
Answer is the biggest hi seen
